corrected_text: ML Drift lowercases AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU, reads underscores as spaces, and matches it against the same name keys as device names ('apple a17 pro', 'apple m2', ...), so a value such as 'A17 Pro' matches no key and leaves AppleGpu::kUnknown; in our build an unknown chip then takes the device's own highest Apple family (capped at Apple10) and an estimated core count (ours: e5e4c6eb; Apple1 in the release Agello ships), so such a value simulates nothing, and our LiteRT reports a kGpuFamilyUnknown anomaly in GpuBackendMetal::GetInfo.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: gpu_info.cc:1372-1385 at b7b856a0 still lowercases the variable and now also turns underscores into spaces (ours: e5e4c6eb, G1); the name table (683-737) still keys on 'apple ...', so 'A17 Pro' leaves kUnknown. New with G1: CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice (environment.mm:42-56) gives an unknown Apple chip the device's highest supportsFamily, capped at Apple10 (DeviceAppleFamily, 33-40), and 6 cores on iPhone, 10 on Mac (SetUnknownChipFamily, gpu_info.cc); so the family is no longer Apple1 in our build. GpuBackendMetal::GetInfo (gpu_backend_metal.mm:204-218) still tests gpu_type == kUnknown and reports kGpuFamilyUnknown. The release Agello ships (6da75396) predates G1: there the family is still Apple1 (git diff 6da75396 b7b856a0 -- gpu_info.cc environment.mm is G1 only).
